cd.method: Preload both pages outside transfer timing. Sender readiness starts at file selection or CLI launch. Receiver timing starts at code entry or CLI launch and ends after browser download save or CLI exit. File and directory fsync added to both; SHA256 checked after timing. Local Worker control and output in tmpfs; not physical persistence. No artificial CPU/decrypt delays.

croc-browser.method: Official croc browser UI and tagged croc-web server, private loopback relay, default browser compression policy. Pages preload outside timing; readiness starts at file selection or CLI launch. Receiver timing starts at code entry or CLI launch and includes automatic consent and download save. File/directory fsync added for every output; SHA-256 checked outside timing. RAM output, warm input cache. No direct browser transport or public internet claim.

method: Alternate CD and croc browser suites, reversing order each round. Both UIs run in the same Chromium version with preloaded pages and private local relays. CD tests direct-allowed and forced-relay routes; croc browser uses its supported WebSocket-to-TCP relay route. Each direction uses random payloads of the same size and entropy class, with independent hashes. File/directory flush and external SHA-256 verification follow each driver. Default browser settings, no profiler. Existing native-croc cross-interface gates remain separate.
